turns.answer: Video A (v1) uses a seafood protein: after a simmered stock is strained and the clear broth is returned to the pot, white ring-shaped seafood pieces are added and simmered/boiled in the liquid. The exact seafood species is not visually resolved. Video B (v2) uses ground chicken as the main animal protein: it is sautéed in a pan with aromatics and scallions as a dry mixture in the observed cooking spans, and later frames show a liquid soup being stirred and served, indicating the chicken preparation is incorporated into a simmered sour soup rather than remaining a dry sauté. Video B also includes tofu among the soup ingredients. Thus the preparations differ in protein—seafood in Video A versus chicken and tofu in Video B—and in cooking method—direct simmering in strained broth in Video A versus dry sautéing followed by soup assembly in Video B.
